description:
The conservative small-count interval: a Clopper-Pearson estimator validated against an independent inversion of its own definition, with empirical coverage demonstrated in the regime the rectangular validation lives in.

## Background

No Clopper-Pearson estimator exists anywhere in-tree, and the rectangular validation cells — where the estimated event probability is of order $q^{-n}$ and counts are in the tens — are exactly where a normal-approximation interval's coverage is weakest. Clopper-Pearson is conservative by construction and keeps its nominal coverage at counts in the tens.

The two estimators answer different questions. Checking one against the other proves nothing — containment follows from how they are built — so this estimator is validated against an independent computation of its own definition, and its coverage is demonstrated empirically rather than assumed from construction.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A Clopper-Pearson interval is returned for a count out of $N$ at a caller-supplied level and matches, to a stated tolerance, an independent computation of its own bounds by inversion of the binomial tail or equivalently by beta quantiles, on cases spanning $Z = 0$, $Z = N$, and counts in the tens.
- [hard] REQ-02: Coverage is demonstrated empirically: over repeated simulated draws at stated $(N, p)$ including small $N$ and small $p$, the fraction of intervals containing $p$ is at least the nominal level.
- [hard] REQ-03: The estimator returns a well-formed interval at $N = 2 \times 10^{7}$, with no overflow, no interval of negative width, and no bound outside $[0,1]$.
- [hard] REQ-04: Documentation states which estimator suits which regime, so a caller at counts in the tens is not left with the normal-approximation interval by default.

## Notes

Entry points take counts, not samples, matching the Wilson estimator beside it, so both are usable online against a running accumulator and offline against a published dataset.
title: Clopper-Pearson interval estimator with coverage demonstration
